newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower, specs sell near close.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower, specs sell near close.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled weaker and near the lows after speculative selling pressured prices near the close, market sources said.
The light selling coupled with a dearth of buying and thin volume pushed May to a low of 83.50 cents. The contract settled at 83.70 cents, down 1.10.
"There is just no interest in the buy side," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
Futures volume was estimated at 1,200 lots compared to Thursday's official 1,786 lots. Options volume was estimated at 1,700 lots.
Support was seen at 80.00 and then 77.50 cents in May. Resistance remained at Wednesday's high of 86.90 and then 88.50, the high made on March 5.
While some market sources were encouraged by Thursday's stronger-than-expected weekly movement data, Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said demand remains weak.

The Florida Citrus Processors Association put frozen concentrated orange juice movement into trade channels for the week ended March 15 at 6,121,429 gallons compared to 5,215,248 gallons the previous week.
Imports were 743,141 gallons compared to 424,913 gallons.
"Sources indicate that a part of this keen demand has been Brazilian low ratio product brought into the state for blending purposes and then shipped to the northeast," Ganes said in a weekly comment.
The Brazilian Association of Citrus Exporters said late Thursday that output could reach 1,089,579.4 metric tonnes 66 Brix in 1996/97, up from 973,306.9 metric tonnes the previous year.
Reports from Brazil earlier in the week indicated that supplies would remain strong through the 1997/98 marketing year. Florida output is also seen climbing to record levels.
In the near term, benchmark May is expected to remain an 80.00 to 85.00-cent trading range.
